scope: Agent visual inspection of all 13 actual Godot Web screenshots, plus deterministic runtime assertions; not a blind user-recognition study.

observations.result: All 32 figures, their pedestals, river and palace remain visible in iso/top/front/side views. Canvas fills the host width after viewport expansion.
In the label-free top view the advisor has a broad horizontal headdress while the soldier has a circular helmet with a single side shield. The distinction survives board-scale rendering.

Inspected both colors at 0.5833334 seconds from four views. Spear, shield, limbs and pedestal remain coherent without visible detached geometry; side views clearly show the spear extended in the attack direction.
Both colors keep the victim at 0.5666667 seconds and hide it at 0.5833334; 14 local bone rotations differ from the starting pose; undo restores four models and resets the motion display.

Final export uses a warmer golden board, darker grid lines and reduced lighting; grid, character outlines and team colors remain clear. It is a simple Godot comparison environment, not visual parity with Three.js.
The final merged grid matches the earlier palace, river and marker geometry in all four views; no missing or displaced line segments observed.

resolvedFindings: Reused piece IDs originally kept the wrong model when switching to demo; type/color identity changes now rebuild the node.
Undo/restart originally restored stale end-of-animation UI through metrics; only active motion metrics now update it.
limitations: No mobile or Safari acceptance was requested or performed.
This is functional Web renderer validation and does not establish comparative performance against Three.js.
Visual inspection is limited to the recorded desktop viewport and sampled animation poses.
